note: Reported cohorts are very small (e.g., 4 to 12 patients), with functional assays showing varying degrees of loss-of-function/splicing disruption, supporting the hypothesis that small cohort sizes currently hinder definitive genotype-phenotype correlation.

evidence.text: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 (three missense and one nonsense variant) were characterized in only four patients from three unrelated families, causing microcephaly, intellectual disability, brain anomalies, and seizures in half the patients.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Herein, we describe the identification of biallelic variants in GTF3C3, which encodes a key component of the TFIIIC subunit, in four patients from three unrelated families of different ethnicities collected through GeneMatcher... Exome/genome sequencing revealed four different GTF3C3 variants including three missense (p.Cys172Gly, p.Val427Phe and p.Ala509Thr) and one nonsense variant (p.Arg717Ter).

evidence.text: In a cohort of twelve affected individuals across seven families, recessive missense variants showed loss-of-function in RNA polymerase III reporter assays and splicing defects, presenting with intellectual disability, motor impairments, seizures, and variable facial features.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: Twelve affected individuals from 7 unrelated families were identified with homozygous or compound heterozygous missense variants in GTF3C3... RNA polymerase III reporter assays confirmed that the majority of missense variants resulted in a loss of function.
